segments.zh: 各位英语学习者，大家好。

segments.en: Welcome back to another podcast here with us at EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 欢迎回到 Englishpod 的另一个播客。

segments.en: And today we're bringing you another part of our sports series and this time it's an advanced lesson.
segments.zh: 今天我们为您带来我们体育系列的另一部分，这次是一个高级课程。

segments.en: We're heading to the mountains today to take a skiing lesson.
segments.zh: 我们今天要去山上上滑雪课。

segments.en: Alright, so we're going to be learning about skiing, a winter sport and very popular throughout the world.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我们将学习滑雪，这是一项冬季运动，在世界范围内非常受欢迎。

segments.en: But before we get started, why don't we take a look at a couple of words in Vocabulary Preview.
segments.zh: 但在我们开始之前，我们为什么不看看词汇预览中的几个单词。

segments.en: Alright, so we're going to hear these two words in our dialogue.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我们将在对话中听到这两个词。

segments.en: The first one is fresh powder.
segments.zh: 第一个是 fresh powder（粉雪）。

segments.en: We probably know this phrase already.
segments.zh: 我们可能已经知道这句话了。

segments.en: Yeah, but here we're talking about fresh light snow.
segments.zh: 是的，不过这里说的是刚下的、松软的雪。

segments.en: So fresh light snow, snow that recently fell.
segments.zh: 也就是刚下的、松软的雪。

segments.en: Okay, so it looks like powder.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以它看起来像粉末。

segments.en: The best kind for skiing on.

segments.zh: 好吧，所以就是 fresh powder（粉雪）。

segments.en: Well, we're also going to meet a four-time giant slalom champion.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们还会见到一位四届大回转冠军。

segments.en: Alright, a four-time giant slalom champion.
Okay, so giant slalom is a type of ski race.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以巨型回转是一种滑雪比赛。

segments.en: When you probably see it on TV when they go down the hill and they have to go through these red or blue flags, right?
segments.zh: 当他们下山时，您可能会在电视上看到它，他们必须穿过这些红色或蓝色的旗帜，对吧？

segments.en: Now, four-time giant slalom champion means he won the giant slalom four times.
segments.zh: 现在，四次大回转冠军意味着他四次赢得了大回转。

segments.en: That's an interesting way of saying that somebody did something many times.
segments.zh: 这是一种有趣的说法，有人做了很多次。

segments.en: So I can say the three-time Nobel Prize winner.
segments.zh: 所以我可以说三届诺贝尔奖获得者。

segments.en: Or the five-time Olympic gold medalist.
segments.zh: 或五届奥运会金牌得主。

segments.en: So now it's time for us to go to the mountains with our famous Rick Fields and Bob Copeland and we'll see what happens.
segments.zh: 所以现在是我们带着著名的 Rick Fields 和 Bob Copeland 去山上的时候了，我们会看看会发生什么。

segments.en: Welcome, ski lovers of all ages.
segments.zh: 欢迎所有年龄段的滑雪爱好者。

segments.en: My name is Rick Fields and here with me is the man that needs no introduction, Bob Copeland.
segments.zh: 我是瑞克·菲尔兹，身边这位不用我介绍了：鲍勃·科普兰。

segments.en: What a beautiful day here in Aspen, Colorado, where the sun is shining and we've got 12 inches of fresh powder.
segments.zh: 科罗拉多州阿斯彭今天天气真好，阳光明媚，还新下了十二英寸厚的粉雪。

segments.en: It doesn't get much better than this.
segments.zh: 没有比这更棒的滑雪天气了。

segments.en: But today we have a special treat for our viewers.
segments.zh: 今天我们还为观众请来了一位特别嘉宾。

segments.en: We're joined here by Ian Russe, four-time giant slalom champion.
segments.zh: 四届大回转冠军伊恩·鲁斯也在现场。

segments.en: And on this special edition of the show, Ian is going to teach us the basics of skiing.
segments.zh: 这期特别节目里，伊恩要教大家滑雪入门。

segments.en: Well, first off, let's get those boots on.
You're going to want to make sure your boots fit snugly.
Now snap them into your bindings.
And you're also going to want a good pair of goggles to protect your eyes.
segments.zh: 还要戴一副好雪镜保护眼睛。

segments.en: It's a bright day today, so there's going to be a lot of glare out there on the slopes.
segments.zh: 今天阳光很强，雪道上会很晃眼。

segments.en: We don't want you hitting any of those moguls.
Bob, since you're a beginner skier and might take a few spills, it's a good idea to have a good warm pair of dry ski gloves.
segments.zh: 鲍勃，你刚学滑雪，可能会摔几跤，最好戴一双干燥保暖的滑雪手套。

segments.en: Well, let's head over onto the chairlift and test your skills.
segments.zh: 走，上缆车，看看你学得怎么样。

segments.en: All right, we're up here on the bunny hill.
segments.zh: 好，我们来到初学者坡道。

segments.en: So Bob, why don't you do a few snowplow turns?
segments.zh: 鲍勃，来几个犁式转弯吧。

segments.en: Well, see that bump over there?
segments.zh: 看见那边那个坡包了吗？

segments.en: I'm going to catch some major air.
Well, thanks for joining us here today.
segments.zh: 好吧，感谢您今天加入我们。

segments.en: I think that about does it.
segments.zh: 今天的节目就到这儿吧。

segments.en: Bob, Ian, time for some après-ski?
segments.zh: 鲍勃，伊恩，滑完雪去喝一杯？

segments.en: We're off to grab some freshies.
segments.zh: 我们还要去滑刚下的粉雪呢。

segments.en: Pretty embarrassing for Rick there, wasn't it?
segments.zh: 这对瑞克来说挺尴尬的，是吧？

segments.en: Yeah, he was a little bit cocky and then he ended up falling.
segments.zh: 是的，他有点自大，然后他最终摔倒了。

segments.en: Well, I think there's a lesson in that for all of us, but what the real lesson is today is language.
segments.zh: 好吧，我觉得这对我们所有人都是一个教训，不过今天真正的课程内容是语言。

segments.en: So why don't we start with language takeaway?
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不从语言要点开始呢？

segments.en: All right, on language takeaway today, let's take a look at the first word.
segments.zh: 好吧，关于今天的语言要点，让我们来看看第一个单词。
我们先来看 bindings（固定器）。

segments.en: Bindings are sort of like a lock that attaches your boot to your ski.
segments.zh: 固定器有点像把雪靴固定在滑雪板上的锁扣。

segments.en: I guess it comes from the verb to bind.
Yeah, to tie something so that it stays.
segments.zh: 是的，把东西系起来，这样它就可以了。

segments.en: So for example, my bindings are broken.
And another piece of skiing equipment and very important is goggles.
segments.zh: 另一件非常重要的滑雪设备是护目镜。
好的，我们现在有护目镜。

segments.en: Not to be confused with Google.
It's spelled almost the same way, huh?
segments.zh: 它的拼写方式几乎相同，对吧？

segments.en: But goggles are kind of like, imagine a big pair of glasses that you wear when you ski.
segments.zh: 但是护目镜有点像，想象一下你滑雪时戴的一副大眼镜。

segments.en: So it makes people kind of look like flies.
segments.zh: 所以它让人们看起来像苍蝇。
他们有这些巨大的眼镜。

segments.en: And you'll also see safety goggles, which you might wear if you are a mechanic fixing a car or someone working with wood or chemicals or what have you.
segments.zh: 你还会看到安全护目镜，比如修车技师，或者接触木材、化学品之类的人就会戴。

segments.en: Okay, so goggles basically protect your eyes from snow, from the sun, from anything.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以护目镜基本上可以保护你的眼睛免受雪、太阳的影响。

segments.en: So moving on to our next ski word.
segments.zh: 所以继续我们的下一个滑雪词。

segments.en: They said you should wear the goggles so that you don't accidentally go over the moguls.
segments.zh: 他们说你应该戴上护目镜，这样就不会不小心越过雪包。

segments.en: Basically these are the bumps that are in a ski hill.
segments.zh: 基本上就是滑雪场里的那些小雪包。

segments.en: Okay, so they're kind of like mini little hills.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以它们有点像迷你小山丘。

segments.en: And they're very difficult to ski over, right?
segments.zh: 而且它们很难滑雪，对吧？

segments.en: You got to be pretty good to handle those moguls.
segments.zh: 要能驾驭那些雪包，你得相当厉害。

segments.en: Now, since these guys are beginner skiers, they're starting out on the bunny hill.
segments.zh: 现在，由于这些人是初学者滑雪者，他们开始在兔子山上。
在滑雪者中非常受欢迎。

segments.en: The bunny hill is the easiest hill.
segments.zh: 兔子山是最简单的山丘。

segments.en: So it's where the beginners start to learn.
segments.zh: 所以这是初学者开始学习的地方。

segments.en: All the kids are on the bunny hill.
segments.zh: 所有的孩子都在兔子山上。

segments.en: Actually, we're going to look at two words here because they mean almost exactly the same thing.
segments.zh: 实际上，我们将在这里看两个词，因为它们的意思几乎完全相同。

segments.en: We heard the ski instructor say gnarly.
segments.zh: 我们听到滑雪教练说 gnarly（超猛）。

segments.en: Okay, but you don't say gnarly.
segments.zh: 好吧，但你并不是那样念的。
还有一个相关的词：sick（超赞）。

segments.en: Now, sick means to be sick, right?
segments.zh: 现在，生病的意思是生病，对吧？

segments.en: Let's listen to some examples to help us understand.
segments.zh: 让我们听一些例子来帮助我们理解。

segments.en: Those were some sick dance moves.
Jack and I went to the beach yesterday and surfed some really gnarly waves.
segments.zh: 杰克和我昨天去了海滩，冲了几道超猛的海浪。

segments.en: Man, the concert last night was sick.
segments.zh: 老兄，昨晚的演唱会太赞了。

segments.en: I can't believe we got front row seats.
segments.zh: 我不敢相信我们有前排座位。

segments.en: So, basically, gnarly and sick, they mean that it's amazing, it was cool.
segments.zh: 所以，gnarly 和 sick 基本上就是说很棒、很酷。

segments.en: So, these two words are very, very informal.
segments.zh: 所以，这两个词是非常非常非正式的。

segments.en: Both of these words, I think, originated with skiers, snowboarders, skateboarders.
segments.zh: 我认为这两个词都起源于滑雪者、滑雪板爱好者、滑板爱好者。

segments.en: So, that's all the words we have for language takeaway, but we have some great phrases that we want to take a look at before we listen to the dialogue again.
segments.zh: 所以，这就是我们为语言要点所拥有的所有词，但在我们再次听对话之前，我们有一些很棒的短语，我们想看看。

segments.en: So, it's time now for Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 所以，现在到了流利表达（流利表达）环节。

segments.en: So, Rick said that it is time to...
So, Rick invited everyone to start skiing by saying, let's hit the slopes.
segments.zh: 所以，瑞克招呼大家开滑，说了句 let's hit the slopes。
所以，hit the slopes 的意思是……

segments.en: Now, we want to hit the slopes.
segments.zh: 现在，我们说 hit the slopes。

segments.en: Now, we can change the noun slope for something else, right?
segments.zh: 现在，我们可以把 slope 这个名词换成别的，对吧？

segments.en: You can change it for a lot of other different nouns.
segments.zh: 您可以将其更改为许多其他不同的名词。

segments.en: And why don't we hear some examples of how you can do that?
segments.zh: 为什么我们没有听到一些关于如何做到这一点的例子？

segments.en: I really have to hit the books and study for my exam tomorrow.
segments.zh: 我真的得啃书本，准备明天的考试了。

segments.en: I think I'm going to hit the bed now.
Honey, can we hit the supermarket on our way home?
segments.zh: 亲爱的，我们可以在回家的路上去超市吗？

segments.en: I need to buy some milk.
So, great examples and now we understand how we can use the hit the something.
segments.zh: 所以，例子很好，现在我们明白怎么用 hit the + 某物 这个说法了。

segments.en: Well, Rick warned Bob that he might take a few spills.
segments.zh: 好吧，瑞克提醒鲍勃，他可能会摔几跤。
所以，take a spill 就是……

segments.en: It means like a light fall or...
segments.zh: 意思就是轻轻摔一下，或者……
对，也可能是摔得挺惨的那种。

segments.en: So, for example, instead of saying, that little girl was riding her bike and she fell, I can say, that little girl was riding her bike and she took a bad spill.
segments.zh: 所以，比如说，与其说那个小女孩骑车时摔倒了，我可以说那个小女孩骑车时摔得很惨。
所以，take a spill 就是……

segments.en: You have to use the verb take though.
You have to take a spill.
Well, you might take a spill when you catch some major air.
segments.zh: 好吧，当你腾空跳起（catch some major air）时，可能会摔一跤。
那么，我有没有抓到什么？
怎么叫 catch air 呢？

segments.en: Well, imagine if you're jumping and your skis are catching the air.
segments.zh: 好吧，想象一下，你跳起来，滑雪板腾在空中。

segments.en: So, I'm in the air for a very long time maybe?
segments.zh: 所以，我可能在空中待了很长时间？

segments.en: When you catch some air, basically, it's like you're flying for a couple of seconds.
segments.zh: catch some air 基本上就是你腾空飞了几秒钟。

segments.en: So, you're flying for a couple of seconds.
You're very high up in the air.

And you'll hear this phrase when you're, you know, not only when you're talking about skiing, but also maybe if you're, you know, you're driving your car really fast and it sort of jumps up in the air for a minute, well, not a minute, a second, that would be catching air as well.
segments.zh: 当你在谈论滑雪时，你会听到这句话，你知道，如果你是，你知道，你开车的速度非常快，它会在空中跳跃一分钟，好吧，不是一分钟，一秒钟，那将是 也吸风。
所以，catch air 就是腾空飞起。

segments.en: They were kind of tired and he said, well, let's call it a day.
segments.zh: 他们有点累，他说，好吧，让我们收工吧。

segments.en: Let's call it a day and go home.
And not before we go to our next word, to grab some freshies.
segments.zh: 在进入下一个词之前，我们还有 to grab some freshies。

segments.en: Remember we talked about fresh powder?
segments.zh: 还记得我们谈过新鲜粉末吗？

segments.en: So, it's an informal way of saying fresh powder.
segments.zh: 所以，这是 fresh powder 的一种非正式说法。

segments.en: So, the snow that nobody has skied on before.
segments.zh: 也就是还没人滑过的雪。

segments.en: Really good phrases and some amazing vocabulary.
segments.zh: 非常好的短语和一些惊人的词汇。

segments.en: Let's listen to this dialogue one last time and then we'll come back and talk a little bit more about this really fun sport.
segments.zh: 让我们最后一次听听这个对话，然后我们会回来多谈谈这项非常有趣的运动。

segments.en: Welcome ski lovers of all ages.
segments.zh: 欢迎所有年龄段的滑雪爱好者。

segments.en: My name is Rick Fields and here with me is the man that needs no introduction, Bob Copeland.
segments.zh: 我是瑞克·菲尔兹，身边这位不用我介绍了：鲍勃·科普兰。

segments.en: What a beautiful day here in Aspen, Colorado, where the sun is shining and we've got 12 inches of fresh powder.
segments.zh: 科罗拉多州阿斯彭今天天气真好，阳光明媚，还新下了十二英寸厚的粉雪。

segments.en: It doesn't get much better than this.
segments.zh: 没有比这更棒的滑雪天气了。

segments.en: But today we have a special treat for our viewers.
segments.zh: 今天我们还为观众请来了一位特别嘉宾。

segments.en: We're joined here by Ian Russe, four-time Giant Slalom champion.
segments.zh: 四届大回转冠军伊恩·鲁斯（Ian Russe）也加入了我们。

segments.en: And on this special edition of the show, Ian is going to teach us the basics of skiing.
segments.zh: 这期特别节目里，伊恩要教大家滑雪入门。
所以，let's hit the slopes（上雪道吧）。

segments.en: Well, first off, let's get those boots on.
You're going to want to make sure your boots fit snugly.
Now, snap them into your bindings.
segments.zh: 现在，把它们卡进固定器里。

segments.en: And you're also going to want a good pair of goggles to protect your eyes.
segments.zh: 还要戴一副好雪镜保护眼睛。

segments.en: It's a bright day today, so there's going to be a lot of glare out there on the slopes.
segments.zh: 今天阳光很强，雪道上会很晃眼。

segments.en: We don't want you hitting any of those moguls.
Bob, since you're a beginner skier and might take a few spills, it's a good idea to have a good warm pair of dry ski gloves.
segments.zh: 鲍勃，你刚学滑雪，可能会摔几跤，最好戴一双干燥保暖的滑雪手套。

segments.en: Well, let's head over onto the chairlift and test your skills.
segments.zh: 走，上缆车，看看你学得怎么样。

segments.en: All right, we're up here on the bunny hill, so Bob, why don't you do a few snowplow turns.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们到了初学者坡道，鲍勃，来几个犁式转弯怎么样。

segments.en: Well, see that bump over there?
segments.zh: 看见那边那个坡包了吗？

segments.en: I'm going to catch some major air.
Ha ha ha, he lost his skis.
segments.zh: 哈哈哈，他的滑雪板丢了。

segments.en: Well, thanks for joining us here today.
segments.zh: 好吧，感谢您今天加入我们。

segments.en: I think that about does it.
segments.zh: 今天的节目就到这儿吧。

segments.en: Bob, Ian, time for some après-ski?
segments.zh: 鲍勃，伊恩，滑完雪去喝一杯？

segments.en: We're off to grab some freshies.
segments.zh: 我们要去滑刚下的粉雪。

segments.en: We heard the guys talk about après-ski, and actually this is one of my favorite parts of skiing.
segments.zh: 我们听到这些人谈论滑雪后，实际上这是我最喜欢的滑雪部分之一。

segments.en: I guess the Frenchness sort of gives it an air of specialness, right?
segments.zh: 我想这股法国味儿让它显得有点特别，对吧？

segments.en: But après-ski is basically the party that you have after you're finished skiing.
segments.zh: 但滑雪后基本上是滑雪后的派对。

segments.en: So usually you would have parties after skiing.
segments.zh: 所以通常你会在滑雪后举办派对。

segments.en: Right, so you finish your ski day, you've called it a day, you've glided down those slopes and you head on over to the lodge, the little cabin, grab a beer or two or maybe some hot alcoholic drink and kick back and relax with your friends.
segments.zh: 对，所以你滑完一天的雪，收工之后，沿着雪道滑下来，然后走向度假小屋，喝上一两杯啤酒，或者来点热饮酒，和朋友一起放松休息。

segments.en: Wow, so it's popular for families to go to a ski resort and stay there for a couple of days.
segments.zh: 哇，所以家庭去滑雪胜地并在那里逗留几天是很受欢迎的。

segments.en: So this is when you would do this with your friends or family.
segments.zh: 所以这是你和你的朋友或家人一起做这件事的时候。

segments.en: If it's with your friends, it's going to last until late into the night.
segments.zh: 如果是和你的朋友在一起，它会持续到深夜。

segments.en: All right, so it sounds fun.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以听起来很有趣。

segments.en: And next time maybe if you go skiing with your friends and you guys are speaking English now, you can use all these great phrases and maybe surprise your friends if you tell them, let's go grab some freshies or something like that.
segments.zh: 下次如果你和朋友一起去滑雪，而且你们现在都在说英语，就可以用上这些很棒的短语，比如跟他们说 let's go grab some freshies 之类的话，让朋友们吃一惊。

segments.en: Yeah, you'll sound pretty, pretty dialed, pretty cool.
segments.zh: 对，你会显得很在行、很酷。

segments.en: All right, so that's all the time we have for today.
segments.zh: 好吧，这就是我们今天所拥有的所有时间。

segments.en: Be sure to check out our website englishpod.com.
segments.zh: 请务必查看我们的网站 Englishpod.com。

segments.en: Marco and I are always around to answer your questions and well, thanks for downloading.
segments.zh: Marco 和我总是随时回答您的问题，感谢您的下载。
